summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analyzing the confidential launch data, building a general recheck-and-act agent product (Lighthouse) with a polished UI, and preparing a demo, hosting and hand-in by 12:45.
summary.outcome: Found the Collector's Edition shortfall (overbooked art books, failed statues, packing speed, sleeve revision) and a 14:37 drop, then built and polished the Lighthouse app (poller, agents, case flow, routines, bell, logo) and hosted an open demo at lighthouse.stenglein.dev. Demo story state is saved and the latest commits are made, but `main` (~30 commits ahead) is not pushed and live is not restarted.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) with no webhooks; changes must be detected by polling the file list and comparing SHA-256, since files are replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data and findings live in the gitignored `data/` folder; `.env` is gitignored and `.env.example` is committed.
The team uses CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md for workflow; tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md, and Entire only checkpoints when repo files change.
The API does not load `.env` on import, so settings like ASK_VIEWER_TITLE need a helper that loads `.env` first or they are missing after restart.

Routine steps are only valid for certain watched kinds (chase-once needs messages awaiting an answer, ask-for-status needs shipments); the server rejects others with 'step N cannot be done on open decisions'.
scripts/demo.sh manages the demo instance: ASK_DEMO_OPEN=on ASK_DEMO_HOST=... restart for open mode, plus save-story/story to snapshot and reset the demo state.
The case-flow connectors and boxes are exported from FlowGraph.tsx and shared with the Routines diagram so they cannot drift apart.

Live (ask-soony.stenglein.dev, password, real email) and demo (lighthouse.stenglein.dev, open, email only recorded) both run on the Mac via a Cloudflare tunnel in tmux; they pick up new web builds but need a restart for server-side changes.

code.finding: Top bar uses a 3-column grid with the heartbeat in the first column and an equal-width side column so the centred status cannot run under the menu; the role chip shows only on very wide screens, and the logo mark was nudged up 2 px to centre with the text (measured row 34.5).

workflow: Measuring rendered pixels (ink positions) settles visual alignment questions faster than guessing nudges.
Screenshotting desktop and phone widths after every UI change caught layout issues (two-column flow reading order, overlapping phone bar, crowded top bar).
Interrupting a tool call does not always stop it: commits went through before the user's stop twice, so check git state afterwards.
Long-running analysis (cross-checking 200 order confirmations and 59 scans) was delegated to a subagent, and the logo variants were drawn by another.
Restarting the Cloudflare tunnel drops all hosts; use the exact tmux session name and verify every host afterwards.

friction: The first tunnel restart failed (tmux did not recognise the session name) and the Ctrl-C stopped the tunnel, taking all three addresses down (530) for about a minute.
The demo instance had lost the rehearsed cases (only 5 open) and had to be reset to its snapshot.
The flow layout took several iterations (two-column snake confusing, phone showing identical compact and detail views, auto-scroll to the case list on load).
'Chase once if no answer' looked broken because the Add-step menu offered it on routine kinds where the server refuses it.
Logo centring needed measurement; the first nudge went in the wrong direction.
The hand-in time moved from 12:00 to 12:45 mid-session, and pushes were repeatedly held back awaiting approval.
The portal login ended up in Discord history, which the assistant flagged as worth changing after the hack.
open_items: Push `main` (~30 commits ahead of origin) before the 12:45 hand-in.
Restart live so the sign-in choice, Felix's Senior Buyer title, heartbeat and new logo on sign-in appear there.
Record the roughly 2.5 minute demo video (user records; data prepared with `scripts/demo.sh story`) and confirm the deck is covered.
Support 'send email, then chase once if no answer' on decision routines (needs a follow-up watching replies).
Rework Routines into a compact list with details on demand, a ⋯ menu and duplicate-routine detection.
Possibly make 'All cases' on phones a bottom sheet opened from the top bar's decision count.
Register sender email addresses in the portal Settings so supplier emails (Karton Nowak art books, 24 h offer; Boise EXW reply) can be sent for real.
Ask the Lio engineers whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create files.
Consider moving the demo to ada so it survives the laptop closing (about 30 minutes, risky before hand-in).
Add a preview image inside the case flow (only 'Open' links exist now).
Decide on or revisit the chosen logo (variant 3 applied), and check that the folded flow view's shorter connectors look right.
